title: SECOND UNIT — Render Farm Ops Wall
description: Importable dashboard for the Grafana track submission. Install this into your own Grafana Cloud stack (Dashboards -> New -> Import -> upload this file) to see the backlot's real Prometheus/Loki/Tempo signal, plus the annotations and incidents SECOND UNIT writes back at runtime.

panels.title: CPU utilization by job
panels.description: This stays GREEN during a low_samples or break_texture condition — the job succeeds normally. That's the whole point: metrics alone cannot see these defects.

panels.title: Renderer logs (Loki)
panels.description: OTLP logs are labeled service_name, not job — matches the resource attribute render_worker.py sets in telemetry.py, not the old (unused) Promtail-style job label this panel originally queried.

panels.title: SECOND UNIT annotations & incidents (written back at runtime)
panels.description: Every annotation and incident here was created by ActuatorAgent after a human approved the plan — this panel is the write-back proof, not a claim.

panels.title: Agent reasoning traces (Tempo)
panels.description: google-adk auto-instruments every sub-agent (invoke_agent <name>), model call (call_llm/generate_content), and tool call (execute_tool) as a real span with the model's actual response text attached — so this is the agent's own reasoning, in Tempo, debuggable the same way any other farm service is. No custom instrumentation needed: this is ADK's built-in OpenTelemetry support, verified live against this stack.

panels.title: Visual defects detected (vision agent verdicts)
panels.description: The payoff of the whole vision-agent idea as a normal Prometheus series: a failure class that CPU/duration/log monitoring structurally cannot see, now a metric you can alert on (see grafana/alerts/) instead of prose in a chat transcript. Emitted by VerdictAgent's after_agent_callback (agent/second_unit/sub_agents/verdict.py) on every diagnose run, live or eval.
